transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 PST | Duration: 62m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Vantis Platform), Derek Lin (Vantis ML), Maya Ortiz (Vantis Prod Ops)

00:00 Speaker 1 - Sara: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run the safety matrix and do a full runbook rehearsal for the pilot cutover, especially the A slash B traffic slices and the circuit breaker thresholds. is that still the right scope for today?
00:22 Speaker 2 - Aisha: yes that works, we have ops standing by and we carved out 2 hours tomorrow for the dry-run but wanted to sync first on the exact gating. quick note, we had one more ingest spike in staging overnight, not sure if that affects the warmup plan.
01:12 Speaker 3 - Miguel: yep saw the spike, likely related to our synthetic generator. for warmup we recommend a warm pool of backends and a prefix KV prime so p95 cold misses drop. we call it warmup pool but it is just a small set of instances to seed the KV cache. you might want 5-10% of expected peak qps for 10 minutes.
02:05 Speaker 2 - Aisha: 5-10% for 10 minutes, okay. are you suggesting dedicated warm instances in the dedicated pool or reused autoscaled instances?
05:00 Speaker 3 - Miguel: reuse autoscaled but prefer reserved min capacity during the window so scaling doesn't kill the warm cache. if you're on the Redwood dedikated plan you can set a min-replicas, otherwise set a steady traffic ramp. small grammar note, the KV cache was transcribed on last call as K V cash in our notes, haha.
12:30 Speaker 1 - Sara: moving on to the safety matrix doc, we split risk into three buckets: functional regressions, latency degradation, and quality regressions. each bucket has trigger thresholds and automatic actions: e.g., quality regressions >3% failure on eval set -> rollback; latency p95 degradation >30% -> traffic fence at 25% and alert runbook.
20:00 Speaker 4 - Derek: on quality regressions, our success criteria are a less than 2% drop on the clinical prompt set and no hallucination increase per the eval harness. can we map the eval hooks to the Redwood Optimize regression alerts? we tried it last sprint but the webhook mapping was a little off.
28:45 Speaker 3 - Miguel: yes we can map eval hooks. i'll send the webhook payload spec; note that webhook retries are 3x with exponential backoff. also recommend putting a short-circuit in the orchestration: if the eval rate falls below X then don't act on it automatically, that prevents noisy signals during low-volume canaries.
35:10 Speaker 2 - Aisha: on A B slicing, can Redwood do staged ramping: start 5% to new variant, after 30 minutes check both telemetry and synthetic smoke, then go to 25%, then 50? how strict are your automated gate checks?
44:00 Speaker 3 - Miguel: we have policy templates. recommended ramp: 5% for 30m with synthetic checks + smoke harness, if p95 and error budget within thresholds and eval delta <2% then 25% for 45m, then 50% for 30m; at each gate there are automatic rollbacks if circuit breaker trips. circuit breaker thresholds: error rate >1% absolute or doubled baseline, or p95 >1.5x baseline. those numbers are configurable per-customer.
50:30 Speaker 1 - Sara: let's rehearse the runbook steps out loud quickly -- step 1: pre-checks (schema, drift, quota). step 2: warmup pool and prime KV. step 3: deploy canary variant to 5% with synthetic, step 4: monitor gates, step 5: ramp if green, step 6: full cutover and blue-green swap, step 7: post-cutover smoke and reconciliation. who wants to read the rollback steps?
58:10 Speaker 5 - Maya: i'll take rollback. rollback step 1: open incident channel and tag all parties, step 2: set traffic to previous stable at 0% for new variant, step 3: disable autoscaler if needed, step 4: run state reconciliation job and regenerate KV if corrupted, step 5: postmortem owner assigned. also note we need a hotfix path for model parameter tweaks without full redeploy.
61:45 Speaker 1 - Sara: great, last bits: security and compliance check - Derek, you asked about audit logs and KMS. Redwood has per-request audit logs, optional retention windows, and KMS integrations; for private we can desktop their HSM. note: the SSO mapping for roles needs env-level RBAC mapping, we'll share the SAML guide.

Recap (automatically generated): agreed runbook rehearsal complete; safety matrix updated with explicit thresholds; synthetic smoke harness is required for 5% gate; warmup pool confirmed; next steps assigned.

Action items (read back): Sarah / Sara to share runbook and observability checklist by 11/05; Miguel to deliver synthetic harness scripts by 11/06; Maya to confirm maintenance window by 11/06; Derek to provide SLO targets by 11/04.

Notes / links shared: Redwood runbook v0.9 (internal link), synthetic-harness repo (sandbox link), telemetry dashboard link (shared view), SAML mapping guide (attachment).

Questions captured: "what if the eval harness shows degradation but telemetry is fine?" -> default: pause ramp and run manual sample evals; "do we need extra contracts for private HSM?" -> yes, procurement path noted.

Meeting close: 15:02 PST - Sara: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the staging dry-run.
